title: Demonstrators clash with police in Paris over living costs and public services
seoTitle: Paris cost of living and public services protest

tea.why: Protesters are demonstrating against rising living costs, declining purchasing power, and worsening conditions in public services and schools.
tea.want: Demonstrators demand relief from economic hardship, better public services, and changes to government spending and policies.
tea.changed: Oct 19: Paris police issued overnight curfews in areas affected by recent rioting, while President Macron rejected the interior minister's resignation.

summary: Nationwide demonstrations in France concerning the rising cost of living, declining purchasing power, and public services escalated into widespread unrest, clashes with police, arson, and looting in Paris and other cities such as Marseille, Lyon, Bordeaux, and Lille. The movement initially developed from weeks of student protests over school conditions and teacher shortages. Organisers and authorities reported hundreds of thousands of participants nationwide. In Paris, demonstrators clashed with security forces who deployed tear gas and water cannons. Authorities reported numerous arrests, injuries among law enforcement personnel, and extensive property damage, including attacks on businesses, public buildings, and a synagogue in the capital's 19th Arrondissement. President Emmanuel Macron and Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu strongly condemned the violence and vandalism, while officials announced localized curfews to curb further disorder.
response: Police deployed tear gas and water cannons, arresting hundreds of individuals in Paris and thousands nationwide. President Emmanuel Macron and Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu condemned the violence, warning that perpetrators would face legal consequences, and local authorities imposed overnight curfews.

crowd.text: about 550,000 people nationwide, according to French authorities

injuries.text: more than 150 police officers were injured

updates.text: Demonstrations over living costs turned violent with clashes, arson, and looting reported across multiple French cities.
Paris police imposed an overnight curfew in affected areas as President Macron rejected the interior minister's resignation.
